minutes.headline: Assessors voted to send estimated third-quarter tax bills; they also discussed lakefront tiers and the five-year recertification.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors heard public comment on how lakefront valuation tiers will be confirmed in the five-year recertification, then reviewed the assessing office's work plan, including new growth, sales verification, mapping and the data collection manual. The board voted to send estimated third-quarter tax bills and later moved to executive session, not to return to public session. Board members also discussed documenting abatement policies and tracking resident complaints and unanswered questions.

public_comment.topic: Praised the assessor's office staff as responsive and helpful after calling that morning.
Asked how inspectors in the five-year recertification will know how to place lakefront properties in the three tiers, and whether a document defines the tiers and who would approve it.
Mr. Luck raised that lakefront properties not included in the abatement review received a tier rating without inspection and have no baseline.

votes.motion: Send out estimated third-quarter tax bills as per the recommendation of the primary assessment.
Move into executive session, not to return to public session afterward.

budget_items.what_was_said: Staff asked the board to vote to send estimated third-quarter bills because the recertification pushback means actual bills will not be ready. The alternative discussed was borrowing.
Discussion of the overlay for abatements and exemptions, and that free cash was used, with a figure mentioned that was garbled.
figures_as_heard: a hundred and sixteen thousand dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: Members asked how big a rate adjustment might be after the estimated bills; a percentage was mentioned but unclear.
Staff described income and asset limits for the elderly and low income exemption.
figures_as_heard: seventy thousand dollars for a couple

decisions.decision: The board acknowledged the lakefront tier parameters need to be codified as an official written policy and voted on, to be made available to the public.
A member offered to work with the office on a project timeline for the five-year review dependencies; the board appeared to accept this.
Staff will look at the complaint log and consider tracking resident questions left unanswered.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted to send estimated third-quarter tax bills, on the recommendation of the primary assessment.
Staff said the recertification pushback means actual bills will not be ready; borrowing was the alternative discussed.
The board acknowledged that the lakefront tier parameters need to be written down as an official policy, voted on, and made public.
A resident asked how inspectors will place lakefront properties in the three tiers, and another said some properties got a tier without inspection.
A member offered to build a project timeline with the office for the five-year review; staff will consider tracking unanswered resident questions.

why_it_matters: Estimated bills mean the third-quarter payment is not based on final values, and a later tax rate adjustment could follow, so residents should expect a possible change when the actual bill is set.
Lakefront owners have no written definition of the three tiers yet, and the tier assigned in the recertification affects their assessed value and any abatement they might seek.
watch_next: A board vote on the written lakefront tier policy, which the board said it would make available to the public.
The size of any tax rate adjustment after the estimated bills, which members asked about but the captions did not make clear.
